subject: Reserved capacity commit - flex request & phased scaling plan
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@novus.ai>, Novus Procurement <procurement@novus.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 05 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Reserved capacity commit - flex request & phased scaling plan

Elena / Procurement team —

Thanks again for the productive call earlier. Novus' projected traffic profile for Q3–Q4 looks spiky (burst windows around product launches) so your ask for a shorter initial committed tenor with an option to step up capacity later makes sense.

Attached is a first-pass phased activation plan that maps commitment buckets to expected GPU SKU mix and corresponding discount tiers. Key asks from our side: a clear trigger for phase 2 activation, and clarity on whether passage of certain usage thresholds can be used to recalibrate committed units (not just billing).

High-level proposal in the sheet:
- Phase 1 (3 months): baseline reserved pool sized for steady-state inference — 120 A100-equivalent units; standard committed discount (10%).
- Phase 2 (months 4–12): staged ramp tied to a mutually-agreed trigger (30% traffic increase OR launch milestone) — additional 80 units; price resets to 12% if triggered within 6 months, 15% if triggered within 3 months.

We want to be explicit about GPU-cost sensitivity: if market cost moves >15% vs. current pricing, both sides will reconvene to re-run the SKU mix and discount math. That prevents either side from being locked into an untenable economics while still giving Novus predictability.

Please review and flag anything you need changed. I copied Karthik and Ben from pricing/finance for initial sizing and to confirm discount bands.

Next step: can we get procurement's sign-off on the triggers and a candidate legal timeline for a limited-term amendment?

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Sales Lead, Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Novus_phased_plan.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Elena Park <elena.park@novus.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Novus Procurement <procurement@novus.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 05 May 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity commit - flex request & phased scaling plan

Naomi —

Thanks for the doc; that phased approach looks workable. A couple of clarifications from procurement: 1) we need an explicit floor so Phase 1 can't be reclaimed to below 90 units, 2) the trigger should be usage-based (30-day rolling average exceeds threshold) rather than milestone-based.

We also need pricing guardrails — Novus cannot accept retroactive price increases that result from GPU market volatility without an agreed cap and an observable index. Novus proposes a 20% cap on price increases for the initial 12-month term and an independent GPU index (we can propose one) to be used for adjustments.

I'll loop the legal team once we settle the cap and the trigger language.

Regards,
Elena
Head of Cloud Ops, Novus AI
elena.park@novus.ai

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 06 May 2026 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Reserved capacity commit - flex request & phased scaling plan

Folks — forwarding Novus' reply. Quick notes from pricing/ops perspective:

- Floor: we can accept the 90-unit minimum if Novus takes a slightly lower initial discount in Phase 1 (8% instead of 10%). That reduces downside while preserving runway to scale.
- Trigger: usage-based 30-day rolling average is reasonable operationally; implementing automated monitoring + a shared dashboard (read-only) handles auditability.
- GPU-index cap: Novus' 20% cap is okay as long as the index is acceptable and a carve-out exists for supply shocks (force majeure pricing spikes >40%).

I need approval to grant an exception for the 8% discount in Phase 1 and to allow legal to draft a narrow GPU-indexed price adjustment clause with a 20% cap and a 40% force-majeure carve-out. If approved, we can push a marked term sheet and the phased activation SOW.

Can Marcus or Grace confirm the approval path for the discount exception (who needs to sign off: Sales VP? CFO?) and whether we should route through commercial review or exec approval?

Thanks,
Karthik
Head of Pricing, Redwood Inference

Thanks for the analysis, team.

Decision: Approve the 8% Phase 1 discount exception and authorize Legal to proceed with a gated GPU-index clause. Conditions:
1) Legal drafts the adjustment clause to reference the agreed external GPU cost index (we'll vet the index with Finance).
2) We include a hard 40% market-spike carve-out for immediate reprice/renegotiation.
3) The Phase 2 trigger and dashboard hook are implemented prior to any Phase 2 activation; activation requires documented trigger verification and a 5-business-day notice window.

Naomi — please update the term sheet and send to Elena + procurement with the marked changes (include the spreadsheet and the sensitivity pdf I attached here). Karthik — loop Finance to validate the index and the math. Grace — please prepare the approval note for the CFO sign-off in case Novus asks for a multi-year extension later.

I'll own exec-level sign-off if Finance confirms index validity.

Marcus Lin
VP, Commercial
Redwood Inference
